# Section IV: driving dataset composition

**Generated by** `scripts/make_dataset_composition.py` from the dataset (read-only); unit = verified fixation scene (322). Tags follow `docs/scene_metadata.md` (schema 2). Shares are of all 322 scenes. Use this to show coverage and balance; it contains no accuracy results.

| Evaluated recordings | 21 (2.00 h) |
| Recording days | 5: 2026-07-15 (50 scenes), 2026-10-14 (6 scenes), 2026-10-15 (96 scenes), 2026-11-04 (114 scenes), 2026-11-11 (56 scenes) |
| Participants | 4: P1, P2, P6, P8 |

## 7. Suggested groupings for the paper

Coarse groups with enough scenes in each cell, for a balance figure or table:

| Dimension | Groups (scenes) |
|---|---|
| Target | licence plate 154 (48%); road sign 96 (30%); traffic light (incl. pedestrian) 72 (22%) |
| Distance | medium (20–40 m) 168 (52%); near (< 20 m) 91 (28%); far (≥ 40 m) 63 (20%) |
| Ego | moving (incl. braking/starting) 243 (75%); standing 79 (25%) |
| Speed (moving scenes) | ≤ 30 km/h 129 (53%); > 30 km/h 114 (47%) |
| Relative motion | target static, ego approaching/passing 186 (58%); target moving 72 (22%); both standing 64 (20%) |
| Side | right side 129 (40%); left side 115 (36%); ahead / overhead 78 (24%) |
| Road | urban 237 (74%); suburban / highway 85 (26%) |
| Exposure | normal 169 (52%); over-exposed (partly/largely) 153 (48%) |

**Balance notes (facts from the tables above):**
- Every coarse group has at least ~18% of scenes except where noted; the sparse cells are pedestrian traffic lights (7), highway (4), side-window gaze (2) and the rarer relative motions (parallel, overtaking, being passed).
- Target class and participant are linked: licence plates come mainly from P1 and P6, road signs mainly from P2 and P6. Compare classes within participants or state this when pooling.
- Speed: GNSS speed for 268 scenes; annotated speed class only for 54 (2026-07-15: 50, 2026-10-14: 4), drives without vehicle data.
- Distance: camera-based for 62 scenes (2026-07-15: 50, 2026-10-14: 4, 2026-10-15: 6, 2026-11-04: 2); LiDAR otherwise.
